geometry_edits.rationale: Convert the split-wing dominant mass into a courtyard macro to establish a public void and clearer neighborhood threshold.
Widen the void to a usable court rather than a decorative notch.
Open the court toward the access side to strengthen the public threshold.
Keep a legible occupied base so the proposal reads as one building with an active street edge.

graph_edits.rationale: Retool the dominant mass into a courtyard-producing macro so the ground threshold and public void become central rather than incidental.
Make the court readable and usable, not a thin split.
Align the public opening to the verified access side so the street edge reads as an entry condition.
Preserve an occupied base to keep the mass anchored at grade and avoid a floating or sealed object.

rationale: The candidate reads as a compact split bar in one view, but the four views do not resolve into a single coherent neighborhood-building gesture. The mass is too generic and box-like, with a shallow split that does not produce a convincing public void or active threshold at the verified access edge. The blue access edge is not answered by a legible entry seam, court, or undercut; instead the frontage feels sealed and semantically indifferent. The top and oblique views also suggest overlapping or colliding solids rather than a continuous sectional rule, which weakens repair integrity and program support. It can plausibly host neighborhood living in scale, but not yet in visible ground/public-space organization.
